executive_assessment.text: Governorate detail differentiates northern drought and flood-service exposure from inland/southern heat; the health brief's 2050 projections are kept distinct from current rural and peri-urban service gaps.

Water scarcity and regional disparities support a bounded national social-conflict pathway. Separate local evidence from Kesra, Oued El Barka and Zaouiet Ben Ammar describes governance and water-reliability gains, not climate-attributed conflict reduction.
Recent national water-scarcity and reform summaries coexist with older meteorological, coastal and groundwater evidence; planned investments and recommendations are not delivered results.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026-06 reports: By 2050, 1.1m people face ≥15-cm flood exposure; highest in Ben Arous, Tunis, Sfax and Nabeul.
Source dated 2026-06 reports: By 2050, annual consecutive dry days may exceed 114; increases largest in Béja, Bizerte and Manouba.

Source dated 2026-06 reports: By 2050, flooding may disrupt up to one-third of emergency services in Bizerte and Manouba, disable Jendouba facilities, and expose primary-care centers in Tunis, Manouba and Ariana.
Source dated 2026-03-19 reports: Kesra water works supported about 100 farmers/20 ha, raised fig-tree density from 40 to 70/ha and created 4,000 workdays.
Source dated 2026-03-19 reports: Kesra established a water association; ILO reports fewer local water conflicts.

Source dated 2026-03-19 reports: Oued El Barka restored water reliability: 120 farmers returned, including 100 smallholders who left land from scarcity; water did not run out during 2021-2023 droughts.
Source dated 2026-03-19 reports: A rehabilitated spring serves 342 Zaouiet Ben Ammar households; the project site was in an area long restricted for military reasons.
Source dated not stated reports: The Sisseb-El Alem aquifer in Kairouan shows a falling piezometric level, which FAO identifies as evidence of high overexploitation.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 20 of 20 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

UNDP explicitly links climate-aggravated water scarcity and regional disparities with social conflict, but its 2020 document gives no named governorate conflict episode and does not establish violent conflict.
ILO reports reduced water-related conflicts alongside project-supported climate resilience, but does not state the conflicts were climate-induced or quantify a before/after trend.
No inspected primary source directly documents insecurity blocking climate adaptation or climate-service access. The ILO military-restriction detail is contextual and not an assessed causal pathway.
The full 92-page World Bank CHVA was not retrieved; claims from that assessment are limited to its five-page French policy brief. The 2021 World Bank Climate Risk Country Profile PDF returned 403.
UNDP water and coastal baselines are mostly from 2015-2019; FAO indicators have mixed vintages; INM's observed temperature period ends in 2012. These are not current trend estimates.
The 2026 World Bank press release summarizes the Tunisia Economic Monitor but does not expose its model assumptions or subnational job and water impacts.

The 2026 health policy brief supplies a 2050 period but does not state the model scenario for population flood, dry-day and heat projections; these are low-confidence summary-level claims, not independently replicated estimates.
Kesra's reported reduction in water disputes is retained as local resilience evidence, not proof that climate caused the disputes or that the intervention's causal impact was identified.
No governorate-specific climate-driven violent incident or reverse insecurity-to-adaptation mechanism was established. Military restrictions around one project village are contextual only.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
